bib.title: InstructBLIP: Towards General-purpose Vision-Language Models with Instruction Tuning

question: Does instruction tuning a BLIP-2 model on many instruction-formatted vision-language datasets produce a general-purpose model that generalises zero-shot to unseen datasets and tasks?
hypothesis: Instruction tuning, plus letting the Q-Former see the instruction, improves zero-shot generalisation over BLIP-2 and over plain multitask training.
contributions: A systematic study of vision-language instruction tuning: 26 datasets in 11 task categories, 13 held-in for tuning and 13 held-out for zero-shot evaluation, with four task categories held out entirely
Instruction-aware visual feature extraction (the instruction is also fed to the Q-Former) and a square-root-size balanced dataset sampling strategy
An open-sourced suite of InstructBLIP models on FlanT5 and Vicuna, with state-of-the-art zero-shot and finetuned results

method.summary: Start from pretrained BLIP-2 (ViT-g/14 image encoder, Q-Former, frozen LLM) and instruction-tune only the Q-Former on 13 held-in datasets turned into instruction templates. The instruction text is fed to the Q-Former as well as the LLM, so the visual features depend on the instruction. Evaluate zero-shot on 13 held-out datasets and finetune on four downstream datasets.
method.task: vision-language instruction tuning (captioning, VQA, video QA, classification, visual dialog)

datasets.name: 13 held-in datasets (COCO Caption, Web CapFilt, TextCaps, VQAv2, OKVQA, A-OKVQA, OCR-VQA, LLaVA-Instruct-150K, plus held-in image question generation built from QA sets)
datasets.size: COCO 82K train images; Web CapFilt 14M image-text pairs; TextCaps 21K train images; VQAv2 82K train; OKVQA 9K train; A-OKVQA 17K train questions; OCR-VQA 800K train; LLaVA-Instruct-150K 23K detailed caption + 77K reasoning + 58K conversation. Per-dataset sampling counts and the exact list of 13 are not given in text
datasets.split: training sets for tuning; validation or test sets for held-in evaluation
datasets.preprocessing: Each task gets 10 to 15 hand-written instruction templates sampled uniformly; 'short'/'briefly' added to some templates; no templates for LLaVA-Instruct-150K; OCR tokens added after the image query embeddings for scene-text datasets

datasets.name: 13 held-out datasets (NoCaps, Flickr30K, GQA, VSR, IconQA, TextVQA, Visual Dialog, HatefulMemes, VizWiz, ScienceQA-IMG, MSVD-QA, MSRVTT-QA, iVQA)
datasets.size: e.g. NoCaps 15,100 images; Flickr30K test 1K images; Visual Dialog val 2,064 images x 10 rounds; MSVD-QA test 13K QA pairs; MSRVTT-QA test 72K; iVQA 2K test
datasets.split: NoCaps val, Flickr30K test, GQA test-dev, VSR test, IconQA test, TextVQA val, Visdial val, HM val, VizWiz test-dev, ScienceQA test, MSVD test, MSRVTT test, iVQA test
datasets.preprocessing: ScienceQA restricted to image-context questions; four task categories held out entirely (visual reasoning, video QA, visual conversational QA, image classification)

datasets.name: ScienceQA IMG, OCR-VQA, OKVQA, A-OKVQA
datasets.split: train for finetuning; ScienceQA test, OCR-VQA test, OKVQA test, A-OKVQA val and test (Table 3)
datasets.preprocessing: image resolution kept at 224x224 during finetuning

models.name: InstructBLIP (FlanT5-XL)
models.params: 3B LLM (4B total as stated in Sec 3.1)
models.architecture: ViT-g/14 image encoder + Q-Former + frozen encoder-decoder FlanT5 LLM

other.trainable: Q-Former only; image encoder and LLM frozen

models.name: InstructBLIP (Vicuna-7B)
models.architecture: ViT-g/14 + Q-Former + frozen decoder-only Vicuna-7B (instruction-tuned LLaMA)
models.init_from: BLIP-2 pretrained by the authors with Vicuna using the same procedure as BLIP-2 (no official checkpoint existed)

models.name: InstructBLIP (Vicuna-13B)
models.init_from: BLIP-2 pretrained by the authors with Vicuna

other.note: numbers taken from Alayrac et al. 2022

training.objective: standard language modeling loss to generate the response given the instruction
training.lr_schedule: linear warmup then cosine decay to minimum learning rate 0
training.steps: maximum 60K steps; validate every 3K steps; one optimal checkpoint selected per model and used for all datasets

other.sampling: dataset d sampled with p_d = sqrt(S_d) / sum_i sqrt(S_i), with manual weight adjustments: A-OKVQA lowered, OKVQA raised (amounts not given)
other.trainable_params_finetuning: 188M (versus 1.2B when the visual encoder is also finetuned, as in BLIP-2/Flamingo)
other.finetuning_hyperparameters: not stated for the downstream finetuning of Table 3

inference.decoding: direct generation for captioning and open-ended VQA; vocabulary ranking (restrict to candidate list, pick highest log-likelihood) for ScienceQA, IconQA, A-OKVQA multiple-choice, HatefulMemes, Visual Dialog, MSVD, MSRVTT
inference.samples: single run per model; no seeds or variance reported
inference.prompting: zero-shot instruction per dataset (Appendix E); options listed as (a) blue (b) yellow ...; binary classification expands labels into verbalizer sets (yes/true, no/false)

parameters.video_frames: 4 uniformly sampled frames per video, each through image encoder and Q-Former, features concatenated before the LLM

metrics.name: Top-1 accuracy
metrics.definition: used for all datasets except NoCaps, Flickr30K, iVQA, HatefulMemes, Visual Dialog

metrics.name: MRR
metrics.definition: Mean Reciprocal Rank for Visual Dialog, chosen over NDCG because NDCG favours generic, uncertain answers

baselines: Previous SOTA finetuned: LLaVA, GIT, PaLM-E (562B), PromptCap, Shao et al. 2023
eval.protocol: zero-shot on held-out sets; ablations on FlanT5-XL and Vicuna-7B; multitask comparison on FlanT5-XL under identical training settings; held-out average for the multitask comparison over GQA, TextVQA, VSR, HatefulMemes, IconQA, ScienceQA, iVQA, VizWiz. No seeds or significance tests.

availability.data: public datasets; instruction templates in Appendix D and E

prompts.purpose: short-answer VQA zero-shot (GQA, VizWiz, iVQA, MSVD, MSRVTT)

prompts.text: <Image> This is an image with: "{}" written on it. Is it hateful? Answer:
<Image> Based on the image, is this statement true or false? "{}" Answer:
<Image>Given the image, generate a question whose answer is: {Answer}. Question:

Zero-shot on MSRVTT-QA, InstructBLIP FlanT5-XXL gets 25.6 against Flamingo-80B at 17.4 and BLIP-2 FlanT5-XXL at 17.4.
results.table: Table 1, row InstructBLIP (FlanT5XXL), column MSRVTT QA

results.setup: downstream finetuning, Table 3; explanation not tested

limits: Authors state the model inherits hallucination and bias from the frozen LLMs and do not recommend downstream use without safety and fairness assessment (Appendix A).
No seeds, variance or significance tests; one checkpoint chosen by validation per model.
Qualitative comparison with GPT-4, LLaVA and MiniGPT-4 uses few hand-picked examples, with responses taken from their papers or demos.
Ablations only on FlanT5-XL and Vicuna-7B and only five held-out datasets; the manual sampling-weight adjustments are not quantified.
The FlanT5 vs Vicuna explanation for multi-choice vs open-ended finetuning differences is asserted, not tested.
Held-out sets were chosen to avoid contamination but the LLM and image encoder pretraining data are not audited.
Dated: Flamingo, LLaVA, MiniGPT-4 and GPT-4 comparisons are from early 2023.

terms.definition: the textual instruction is given not only to the frozen LLM, but also to the Q-Former, so that it can extract instruction-aware visual features from the frozen image encoder
held-in datasets are used for instruction tuning; held-out datasets are for zero-shot evaluation, either seen tasks on unseen datasets or entirely unseen tasks
restrict the model's vocabulary to a list of candidates, compute log-likelihood for each and select the highest
